scan.summary: This is Cascade Specialty Chemicals' own written Emergency Action Plan for the 42-employee Portland facility, describing alarm signals, evacuation routes, assembly point, headcount, and rescue/medical duties. It is a self-authored safety program governed by Oregon OSHA's OAR 437-002-0042, not an agency-issued permit, so the fixes are things the company writes into its own plan rather than conditions imposed by a regulator.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated 'Revised February 2021,' over five years old as of today. Section 6 states the facilities lead reviews the plan every January, but there is no indication in the document that any January review since 2021 produced a revision — either the annual reviews are not happening as described, or they are happening but not being reflected in an updated document. Either way, a current, re-dated version should be requested.

gaps.title: No stated procedure for reporting an emergency
gaps.description: The plan describes the alarm signals and notes that manual pull stations exist at each exit door, but it never states the actual procedure an employee follows to report a fire, chemical release, or other emergency (e.g., who to call, what number, or the sequence of pulling an alarm and notifying a specific person).
gaps.fix: Add a short subsection stating exactly how an employee reports an emergency: e.g., pull the nearest manual station and/or call 911, then notify the facilities lead or incident coordinator by radio/phone.
gaps.quote: Manual pull stations are located at each exit door.

gaps.title: No procedure for shutting down or securing critical equipment before evacuating
gaps.description: Section 3 instructs employees to 'secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds' before evacuating, but the plan gives no procedure for safely shutting down or securing any critical chemical-handling equipment (transfer pumps, reactors, tanks) before leaving, which the rule requires the plan to address one way or another.
gaps.fix: Identify any equipment that needs emergency shutdown before evacuation, assign a specific role to perform it, and describe the steps — or state explicitly that no equipment requires pre-evacuation shutdown and why.
gaps.quote: secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds

gaps.title: No named contact for questions about the plan or employee duties
gaps.description: The plan names functional roles (facilities lead, incident coordinator, floor wardens) but never designates a specific name or job title that employees can contact for more information about the plan itself or their duties under it, as the rule requires.
gaps.fix: Add a line naming a specific job title (e.g., EHS Coordinator or Facilities Lead by name) as the point of contact for questions about the plan and employee duties under it.

facts.affects: Confirms the facility is above the 10-employee threshold under OAR 437-002-0042(1)(b), so a written (not verbal) plan is required, and sets the scope of coverage for training and evacuation duties.

expected_missing.why: Oregon OSHA's companion rule (OAR 437-002-0043) typically sits alongside an Emergency Action Plan for facilities handling chemicals, covering ignition-source control and housekeeping; it is not referenced here.

expected_missing.title: Written Hazard Communication Program
expected_missing.why: A chemical distributor handling SDS-referenced products would normally hold a HazCom program covering labeling, SDS access and training, which this EAP references (bringing the SDS to responders) but does not itself contain.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Drill and training records/log
expected_missing.why: Companies with twice-yearly drills and annual warden/responder training usually keep a dated log or sign-in sheet as evidence, which is not part of this plan.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Spill/release response procedure
expected_missing.why: A chemical distribution site handling releases would typically have a more detailed spill response or SPCC-type procedure beyond the shelter-in-place instructions given here.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
